name: Schofield Barracks
tagline: Home of the 25th Infantry Division, the 'Tropic Lightning' division, in the heart of Oahu.
_note: Army Hawaii (USAG Hawaii), central Oahu. Marked OCONUS (Hawaii PCS is an overseas-style move) but BAH-rated: MHA HI408 (Honolulu County). Facts verified from official sources (home.army.mil/hawaii, islandpalmcommunities.com, tripler.tricare.mil, DeCA/AAFES, Wikipedia for corroborated headline facts). data.Also part of: U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii (with Wheeler, Fort Shafter)

sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Schofield Barracks, established in 1908 next to Wahiawa, is the largest Army post in Hawaii and the place where the 25th Infantry Division, the 'Tropic Lightning' division, was formed in 1941. It sits on the central plateau of Oahu.

It is part of U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii, headquartered at neighboring Wheeler Army Airfield, which also includes Fort Shafter (the Army's Pacific headquarters) and several smaller posts across the island.

source.label: National Archives (2021); army.mil 25th ID history; Move With Aloha (Feb 2026)

sections.title: An Island Assignment: Central Oahu Army Life

data.subtitle: Hawaii is paradise and a logistical puzzle. BAH is high but the cost of living is higher, and from Schofield's central-Oahu perch the commute and climate trade-offs differ from the town-side bases.
intro: A Hawaii tour is a true OCONUS-style move even though it's a U.S. state: household goods ship by sea, you usually bring one vehicle at government expense, and imported goods cost more. On-base housing is often the best value against high island rents.

Schofield sits on the cooler, wetter central plateau: Wheeler averages 42.5 inches of rain a year, against 24.7 at the Honolulu airport. Wahiawa is about 9 minutes from the middle of the post and Mililani about 11 to 12 with no traffic, while Pearl Harbor's Nimitz Gate is about 28 and Tripler about 31. In Hawaii your street address also sets your children's school, with no school choice, so pick the neighborhood with the school in mind.

recommendations.advice: Island Palm Communities, a Centinel community formed in partnership with the Army, runs the Army's Oahu housing. Rent is set from your BAH (some homes carry a special rate) with utilities included. Report to the Army housing office soon after you arrive, even if you plan to live off post: the Army's guide allows 7 workdays, and Military OneSource says five days.
Wahiawa (about 9 minutes) and Mililani (about 11 to 12) are the closest towns. Mililani addresses are in the Mililani school complex; for a Wahiawa address, confirm the assigned school.
Arrange your one-vehicle shipment, expect a sea shipment for household goods, and budget for a higher cost of living than the BAH suggests.
Lyman, McNair, Wheeler's Kunia Gate and Helemano's main gate are open 24 hours; Foote, Macomb and Wheeler's Kawamura Gate keep shorter hours, and Funston is closed.

source.label: USAG Hawaii School Information Handbook (Jan 27, 2026); State of Hawaii Data Book 2024

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Open 24 hours: Lyman (the visitor gate), McNair, Wheeler's Kunia Gate and Helemano's main gate. Foote opens weekdays 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. and weekends 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; Wheeler's Kawamura Gate weekdays 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.; Macomb weekdays 5 a.m. to 1 p.m. plus outbound only 4 to 6 p.m.; Funston is closed. McNair is inbound only from 5 to 6:30 a.m. on weekdays.

Visitors need a REAL ID-compliant ID and a sponsor with a DoD ID. The Lyman Gate Visitor Control Center ((808) 787-0941) is open 24 hours for extended passes; one-day passes come from any Vehicle Processing Center, and visitors can get a pass online at pass.aie.army.mil. Hours change, so confirm on the official site before you go.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-post family housing across the Army's Oahu installations is Island Palm Communities, a Centinel community formed in partnership with the Army; Island Palm says it has more than 7,800 homes at Schofield, Wheeler, Fort Shafter, Tripler, Helemano, Aliamanu and Red Hill. Rent is set from your BAH (some homes carry a special rate), utilities are included, and each family may have up to two pets (some breeds are restricted).

Report to the Army Housing Division (Bldg. 556, 344 Heard Ave, (808) 787-7700) soon after you arrive, even if you plan to live off post (the Army's guide allows 7 workdays; Military OneSource says five days). An undated Military OneSource page says enlisted waits run from immediate to one month and officers' up to 60 days; off post, expect to pay the first month's rent plus a deposit of one month's rent, and to pay utilities yourself.

source.label: Island Palm Communities; USAG Hawaii housing (official)

sections.title: Schools
data: Hawaii runs a single statewide public school system (the Hawaii State Department of Education), and there are no DoD schools anywhere in Hawaii. Your school is set by your street address: there is no school choice, and geographic exceptions are rarely granted.

On Schofield and Wheeler, children attend Daniel K. Inouye, Solomon or Wheeler Elementary (by address) and Wheeler Middle; at Helemano, Helemano or Wahiawa Elementary and Wahiawa Middle. All go on to Leilehua High. In 2025-26 Leilehua High's students were 58% proficient in language arts and 24% in math, with an 89% graduation rate (class of 2025); Mililani High's were 66% and 48%, with 96%.
School Liaison Office: Bldg. 1283, 241 Hewitt St, (808) 787-5644, USAGHI_SchoolLiaison@army.mil. The school bus costs $72 a quarter, round trip.

source.label: Hawaii DOE military families; 2025-26 Strive HI reports (official)

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves. In Hawaii it leans toward renting or living on base for most families, because home prices are among the highest in the country and tours are usually a fixed length.
rent: Your tour is a standard length and your orders feel fixed.
Island home prices are out of reach for your budget, which is common.
On-base housing offers a strong value against high island rents.
You'd rather not manage a high-priced home from afar after you leave.
buy: You expect a long tour or plan to return to or retire in Hawaii.
You can carry Hawaii's high prices and want to build equity with your VA loan.
You're comfortable potentially renting it out at island rates later.
You've found a home and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer, but high prices and fixed tours make on-base or renting the common choice in Hawaii. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, factor the higher cost of living, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: An island PCS has extra logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Allowance (TLA) for OCONUS-style moves; confirm the current rules.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Get on the housing list early
steps.text: Report to the Army housing office (808-787-7700) soon after you arrive, even if you will live off post (the Army's guide allows 7 workdays; Military OneSource says five days), and apply with Island Palm Communities.

steps.title: Sort your vehicle and shipment
steps.text: Track your sea shipment of household goods and your one shipped vehicle; arrange interim transportation and Hawaii registration.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Hawaii uses one statewide system; confirm your assigned school by address and bring records and immunizations.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE enrollment so you can be seen at Tripler Army Medical Center or the Desmond T. Doss Health Clinic.

data.a: The 25th Infantry Division (Tropic Lightning), formed at Schofield in 1941. Schofield is the largest Army post in Hawaii and part of U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii, headquartered at Wheeler Army Airfield, which also includes Fort Shafter.
Yes. A PCS here works like an overseas move (sea shipment, one vehicle, island allowances), though you still receive BAH set by Honolulu County rather than OHA.

On post with Island Palm Communities (rent set from your BAH, utilities included), or off post in Wahiawa (about 9 minutes) or Mililani (about 11 to 12). Your address sets your children's school, and geographic exceptions are rarely granted.
